5) Documentation and usage examples: - user-docs/api-reference.md (section "traceability/valid-annotation-format", lines 109–150): - Documents nested options: - story.pattern and story.example, including default regex equivalent to `^docs/stories/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-DEV-[\w-]+\.story\.md$` and default example "docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md". - req.pattern and req.example, including default regex `^REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+$` and example "REQ-EXAMPLE". - autoFix boolean semantics and default behavior. - Documents flat shorthand options explicitly: - storyPathPattern: shorthand for story.pattern, with precedence rule. - storyPathExample: shorthand for story.example. - requirementIdPattern: shorthand for req.pattern. - requirementIdExample: shorthand for req.example. - Clarifies behavior: - Patterns are regex **sources**; invalid patterns cause a rule configuration error. - When options are omitted, behavior matches earlier versions (backward compatibility). - Pattern checks are additional validation and do not alter auto-fix semantics. - Summarizes how to customize validations via story.pattern/storyPathPattern and req.pattern/requirementIdPattern to match different directory structures or requirement ID schemes. - user-docs/examples.md provides general ESLint usage patterns; combined with API reference option docs and the detailed tests (which act as concrete configuration examples) this meets the acceptance criteria for “clear examples of custom pattern configuration”.

Tests explicitly target all key behaviors (nested vs flat precedence, invalid pattern fallback, example overrides, and integration with existing behavior), and documentation in the API reference explains how to configure these options. With all tests passing, the acceptance criteria and listed requirements for this story are satisfied.
